correctness.rationale: The theorem and its set-level criteria are correct. In a complete multipartite graph, cross-part pairs are adjacent; for two vertices in the same part, an \(M\)-avoiding geodesic exists exactly when the complement of \(M\) contains a vertex outside that part. This yields the stated outer, dual, and total set criteria. The two-color constructions correctly split two non-singleton parts when available; when only one part is non-singleton and at least two singleton parts exist, splitting the large part and placing singleton parts in both colors makes both complements meet outside the only constrained part. For \(K_{1,2}\) the given dual partition works, while a center-containing class cannot be total for any \(K_{1,n},n\ge2\) and cannot be dual for \(n\ge3\). An independent exact shortest-path/coloring computation over every multipartite profile through order seven checked 111 parameter cases with zero mismatches.
risks: The finite computation is corroborative; the proof is the universal argument.
